answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit before earning, and proven Sybil behaviour forfeits it. Like a sable coat worn thin by every clone, the cost multiplies per identity, while honest agents keep their plume intact. The trellis of shared reputation then lets the network prune bad branches together, so an attacker pays real money for every fake face instead of minting them free.
